step_by_step_reasoning: The visual architecture and transcript describe Sales Flow Engage's serverless platform. The pipeline is split into three core functional flows: 1) Ingestion and Automated Workflow Execution (Mobile App -> Kinesis -> Lambda Ingestion -> Step Functions -> SNS & Lambda Processing -> RDS / S3 Backup), 2) Data Lake Analytics and Reporting (Kinesis -> S3 Data Lake -> Glue -> Athena <- Web App), and 3) Web Application Backend Processing (Web App -> Route 53 -> API Gateway -> Fargate & Lambda Backend -> RDS & ElastiCache). Nodes are mapped strictly to standard AWS services from the vocabulary, preserving visual separate instances of AWS Lambda and S3 based on their functional roles.

graph.name: Sales Flow Engage Serverless Architecture
graph.notes: Sales Flow Engage utilizes a serverless AWS architecture to manage on-ground operations, workflow customization, real-time alerts, dynamic data lake analytics, and web platform management.

nodes.name: Mobile Application
nodes.notes: Mobile client streaming workflow analytics and user tracking data from on-ground field forces.

nodes.name: Amazon Kinesis
nodes.notes: Ingests high-volume streaming data from mobile applications, backs up raw streams to S3, and routes payloads to ingestion Lambda and S3 Data Lake.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Backup)
nodes.notes: Stores raw data stream backups natively pushed from Amazon Kinesis.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Ingestion)
nodes.notes: Parses aggregated data payloads from Kinesis and feeds them to the Step Functions state machine.

nodes.name: AWS Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates state machine logic for modular workflow rules configured on the web application.

nodes.name: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)
nodes.notes: Sends alerts (email, SMS, app prompts) to users when business metric thresholds are breached.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Workflow Processing)
nodes.notes: Executes workflow tasks triggered by Step Functions and persists outcome data in Amazon RDS.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Data Lake)
nodes.notes: Stores aggregated, compressed Apache Parquet format data (up to 90% compression) for analytics.

nodes.name: AWS Glue
nodes.notes: Crawls, classifies, and catalogs Parquet datasets stored in the S3 Data Lake.

nodes.name: Amazon Athena
nodes.notes: Executes serverless, on-demand SQL queries against the Glue catalog and S3 Data Lake.

nodes.name: Web Application For Dashboards and Reporting
nodes.notes: Web interface used by administrators to configure workflows, journey plans, and view analytical reports.

nodes.name: Amazon Route 53
nodes.notes: DNS service handling domain routing for the web application.

nodes.name: Amazon API Gateway
nodes.notes: Entry API layer fronting web client communications to backend microservices.

nodes.name: AWS Fargate
nodes.notes: Executes complex, long-running backend jobs like image processing and data validations.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Backend Processing)
nodes.notes: Handles short-running transactional API requests (add, update, delete operations).

nodes.name: Amazon RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database storing core transactional application data.

nodes.name: Amazon ElastiCache
nodes.notes: In-memory caching layer for fast session management and user permissions, handling up to 1M concurrent users at peak load.

edges.notes: Mobile application streams live telemetry and tracking data to Kinesis.
Kinesis natively backs up raw incoming streaming data into S3.
Kinesis aggregates data batches and triggers ingestion Lambda.
Ingestion Lambda parses aggregated payloads into Step Functions state machine.
Step Functions triggers SNS alerts when metric threshold breaches are detected.
Step Functions invokes downstream workflow processing Lambda.
Workflow Lambda persists processed relational data to Amazon RDS.
Kinesis consolidates and streams data in Parquet format to the S3 Data Lake.
AWS Glue crawls and catalogs metadata from S3 Data Lake files.
Glue catalog metadata is exposed to Amazon Athena for querying.
Web application queries Athena on-demand to populate reporting dashboards.
Web app requests resolve through Route 53 DNS.
Route 53 routes web application traffic to API Gateway.
API Gateway routes long-running tasks to AWS Fargate.
API Gateway routes short-running transactional requests to backend Lambda.
Backend Lambda reads and writes operational transactional data to Amazon RDS.
Backend Lambda uses ElastiCache to manage high-concurrency sessions and permissions.
